raw_response:
I’m already old now, so I don’t like taking big risks. This year I will still do mostly what has worked for me before. Cotton is my main crop, and I will keep more land in cotton because I know it better and the buyers are familiar. I’ll keep a smaller piece in stevia to spread the risk and bring some cash if cotton price is not good. I watch what the nearby farmers do, and around here if the spring is normal, cotton goes in after mid-April. I have a well, so I’m not afraid of dry spells, but water costs money, so I won’t irrigate too many times unless the field really looks dry. Fertilizer also costs a lot, so I won’t push too hard. I’d rather use a moderate amount that I can afford and add a little later if the crop looks weak. Family labor is enough for most work, but for busy picking time and some hand work in stevia, I may need to hire a few days.
